prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (operational name Juniper) intakes calls, records/triages/incidents, dispatches, coordinates jurisdictions/shared awareness, monitors policy-threshold surges, and maintains degraded-radio procedures prioritizing emergencies/common picture. Jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local policy and maintain routes/zones to Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center using clinical direction, access, roads, weather, closures, capacity. Ambulance Coordination Platform shares coverage/incidents/availability, tracks positions/status and accepted mutual aid separately, queues outage updates and flags reconciliation; monitor availability, response time, integrity, interfaces. Computer Aided Dispatch Console supports entry/assessment/maps and displays latest confirmed unit status, time/source; staff verify currency. North Gate Status Board and South Gate Status Board show separate access conditions; South Access Lane Notice reports southern constraints. Call Taker Mara (radio alias Larkspur) captures caller/patient details, uncertainty/barriers, pediatric age/weight/caregiver observations; updates before dispatch, produces Caller Location Correction Slip, keeps caller connected when feasible. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield) sets/confirms priority, resolves conflicts, reviews audit memos before duplicate closure, approves/documents overrides and reviews acuity/escalation-risk cases. Data Quality Officer (Pebble) flags/routes defects without changing priority/delaying care; reviews timestamp conflicts and samples records. Regional Medical Director sets/reviews clinical guidance, approves changes within regional authority, advises unusual needs/demand/priorities. Dispatch weighs need, travel, capability, readiness/coverage; records unit, conditions, time/reason/routes and preserves critical coverage. Unit 417 reassigns only if obligations permit and promptly reports last confirmed position/safe status after contact restoration. Fleet Maintenance Cell reports restrictions/radio faults, uses Mutual Aid Release Form, schedules preventive work per manufacturer guidance/history/region; records asset, work, parts, return-to-service. Hospital Liaison Desk contributes relevant review observations while protecting unnecessary information. Kestrel confirms capacity/pediatric limits to dispatch. Mutual aid requests/acceptances use agreed Regional Radio Network call signs; request when local staffed units miss objectives or specialized resources lack. Voice failure: approved data channel if available; timestamp attempts; compare successful checks with planned area intervals. Radio Coordinator uses change card, records channel effective times, reviews South Access Lane Notice; operators announce outages/areas/estimates, crews acknowledge/repeat critical locations/destinations; uncertain crews do not enter where instructions cannot be confirmed. Audit findings identify records, criteria, interpretive limitations; Center retains evidence

New part:
S247: The Regional Dispatch Center provides a periodic summary of assurance activities, open risks, and improvement progress to regional oversight.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
